texts.preamble: Vinod Kumar vs S P Singh on 13 September, 2023 In The Court Of Mr. Sanjay Gargi Principal District & Sessions Judge / New Delhi District Patiala House Courts : New Delhi Fsat No. 10/2022 Cnr No. Dlnd10058542022 In re: 1. Sh. Vinod Kumar S/o Late Sh. Trilok Chand Aggarwal Shop No. 135, Kucha Ghasi Ram Chandni Chowk, Delhi110006. R/o H.No. A5, Rana Pratap Bagh Delhi110 007. 2. Smt. Man Kanwar Kabra W/o Sh. Ram Prakash Kabra M/s Dwarkesh Products E45, Ricco Growth Centre, Hamir Garh Bhilwara, Rajasthan311025. ........ Appellants Versus 1. Sh. S.P. Singh Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi, 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan, Behind Super Bazar Connaught Palace, New Delhi110001. 2. Sh. A.K. Singh Designated Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi, 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan, Behind Super Bazar Connaught Palace, New Delhi110001. .......Respondents Date of Institution : 11.07.2022 Date of hearing arguments : 22.08.2023 Date of Judgment : 13.09.2023 Fsat No. 10/2022 Vinod Kumar & Anr v. Fso & Anr. Page 1 of 10 Appearances: Sh. R.D. Goel, Ld. Counsel for the appellants. Sh. Vinod Kumar Sharma, Ld. Chief Pp for the State/Respondent. Judgment:
texts.facts: BRIEF FACTS: 2. It is stated that on 07.10.2017, Sh. S.P. Singh, the Food Safety Officer alongwith other officials visited the shop no. 135 of Sh. Vinod Kumar S/o Late Sh. Trilok Chand Aggarwal at Kucha Ghasi Ram, Chandni Chowk, Delhi6, The sealed sample packets along with a copy of memo in Form VI were sent to the Food Analyst, Delhi and also to the Designated Officer. An opportunity was given to the appellant/Food Business Operator (FBO) for sending the fourth packet for analysis to NABL accredited Laboratory under Section 47(1)(c)(3) and 2.4.5 of the rule. The Food Analyst analyzed the sample and reported the sample to be misbranded because there was violation of Regulation no. 2.2.1.3 read with 2.3.1.5, 2.2.2.1 & 2.2.2.10 of the FSS (P&L) Regulation vide its Report dated 12.10.2017. The Food Analyst further opined the label of the said article to be misleading as the FSSAI Logo and License Number, list of ingredients and Best Before declaration are not declared on the label. 3. Thereafter, the appellant was provided an opportunity to file an appeal u/s 46(4) of FSS Act within the stipulated period of 30 days, but, no appeal was preferred by the appellants against the report of the Food Analyst. During the course of hearing before the Ld. Adjudicating Officer, appellants herein have submitted their reply on 29.10.2018 denying the charges leveled against them by the FSO. Appellants have stated that the sample commodity is Ayurvedic Proprietary Medicine and their product is not misbranded. The FSO in his counter reply dated 19.12.2018 submitted that Amla Candy is a standardized food article "Candied Fruit" under Regulation No. 2.3.26.1.1 of the Food Safety & Standards (Food Product Standards & Food Additives) Regulation, 2011 and as such, same is covered under FSS Act/Rules/Regulations. Thereafter, Ld. Adjudicating Officer after going through the documents available on record found the appellants guilty for selling 'Misbranded Food Article' in violation of Sections 3(1)(zf)(A)(i)(a), 3(1)(b), 23, 26(1), 26(2)(ii), 27(1), 27(2)(c) & 27(3)(c) of the FSS Act read with Regulation No. 2.2.1.3, 2.2.1.7, 2.3.1.5, 2.2.2.1 and 2.2.2.10 of the FSS (P&L) Regulation, and passed the impugned order dated 07.06.2022 thereby imposing a penalty of Rs.25,000/ & 75,000/ upon the appellant no.1&2 respectively. GROUNDS OF APPEAL: Vinod Kumar vs S P Singh on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91589935/ 2 4. The impugned order is assailed inter alia on the grounds that there is no standard of sweet amla candy under Food Safety Act as it is an ayurvedic product. 5. Ld. Such a standard was prescribed for Chini Dalchini (Cassia lignea) by the Government notification with effect from July 1, 1979 only. 6. Ld. 7. The impugned order is further assailed on the grounds that sanction given by the Designated Officer is bad in law and there was no proper application of mind and consideration of facts by consenting authority; the Adjudicating Officer did not conduct the fair enquiry in a legal way; no departmental witness or other witnesses were examined and that mandatory requirements of the Act have not been complied with. 8. On filing of the appeal, notice was ordered to be issued to the respondent and although no reply has been filed, the present appeal is vehemently opposed. 10. The opinion dated 12.10.2017 of the Food Analyst, Deptt. of Food Safety, Govt. of NCT of Delhi, is as follows : "The sample is misbranded because there is violation of Regulation no. 2.2.1.3 read with 2.3.1.5, 2.2.2.1 & 2.2.2.10 of The Food Safety & Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011." 11. Believing the report of the Food Analyst, the Adjudicating Officer/ADM (Central) has come to the conclusion that Food Business Operator i.e. appellants herein have committed offence of selling misbranded food articles in violation of Sections 23, 26(1), 26(2)(ii), 27(1) & 27(2)(c) of the FSS Act read with Section 3(1)(zf)(A)(i)(a) read with 3(1)(b) of the FSS Act and Section 3(1)(zf)(C)(i) of the FSS Act read with Regulation No. 2.2.1.3, 2.2.1.7 read with 2.3.1.5, 2.2.2.1 and 2.2.2.10 of the FSS Vinod Kumar vs S P Singh on 13 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91589935/ 3 (P&L) Regulation.
texts.arguments: Counsel for the appellant has submitted that Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jagdish Chandra v State of UP SCFAC 19481997 Page 638, has held that the sample was not subjected to any chemical test or analytical process, the opinion of the Public Analyst was not entitled to any weight whatsoever. Furthermore, the Public Analyst revealed in his testimony on the date when the sample was examined, there was no standard prescribed for Chini Dalchini. Counsel for the appellant has further submitted that the standard of one cannot applied to another and in support of that he has relied upon the decision of M.V. Krishna Nambissa v State of Kerala FAC 1979 (I) 72 Supreme Court of India. 12 . The sole contention raised on behalf of appellants is that there is no standard of Sweet Amla Candy under Food Safety Act as it is an ayurvedic product, hence, the order of the Adjudicating Officer is not sustainable. In support of his submission, Ld. Counsel for appellants has relied upon the observation made by the Apex Court in Jagdish Chandra v State of UP (Supra). In this case, the appellant was convicted of a charge that he sold 450 grams of Dalchini for Rs.2.25 to Food Inspector. Even the Food Inspector has admitted that he did not know the distinction between Dalchini proper and ChiniDalchini so called. Counsel for the appellants has further relied upon M.V. Krishna Nambissa v State of Kerala (Supra), where the court has observed that standard of one cannot apply to another. 15. Section 3(1)(zf)(A)(i)(a) of the FSS Act provides that misbranded food means an article of food if it is purported, or is represented to be, or is being offered or promoted for sale with false, misleading or deceptive claims either. It further provides that if the article contained in the package - contains any artificial flavouring, colouring or chemical preservative and the package is without a declaratory label stating that fact or is not labelled in accordance with the requirements of this Act or regulations made thereunder or is in contravention thereof, the same also means misbranded food. Regulation No. 2.2.1.3 of the FSS (P&L) Regulation provides that pre packaged food shall not be described or presented on any label or in any labelling manner that is false, misleading or deceptive or is likely to create an erroneous impression regarding its character in any respect.
